To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Chinese strategic culture is a conceptual map which determines what is a threat and how to deal with it.
Chinese and Western strategic cultures have different conceptions of what constitutes a threat.
Chinese strategic culture is holistic, and the Chinese approach to security is more tolerant of threats than the Western approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the cultural perspective can inform our understanding of the global system, which is a central question in the discipline of International Relations.
the conceptual foundations of the Chinese approach to security and global governance.
the conceptualization of the security of the world system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conception of threat in Chinese strategic culture is more holistic and tolerant of threats than in Western strategic culture.

the conceptual difference in the Chinese and Western strategic culture is not only a matter of different ways of perceiving the world, but more importantly, it is a matter of different conceptual maps of the world.

the Chinese strategic culture is more concerned with the structural balance of the system and is more tolerant of threats that are viewed as something that needs to be eliminated in the Western strategic culture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Chinese strategic culture is not a static and unchanging entity, and it is not a set of beliefs that can be used to predict the behaviour of the Chinese government in a given situation.
we need to develop a new methodology to study Chinese strategic culture, which is based on a more holistic and dialectical approach.
the study of strategic culture should be treated as an interpretative approach to the study of international relations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Chinese strategic culture is not an independent variable in the cause/effect model of international relations.
the cultural perspective is a necessary component of the conceptual map of global governance.
the Chinese approach to global governance is based on a different set of assumptions than those informed by Western culture.
